claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'INSPECT statement, VI-94' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'INSPECT statement, VI-94' then '  Imperative statement, IV-39'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300 dpi render of page 968 (printed B-56) against page-968.md. The markdown carries every entry one per line, in the PDF's order, with sub-entries indented two spaces under their main entry, exactly as printed (e.g. 'INSPECT statement, VI-94' / '  Imperative statement, IV-39'; 'INPUT phrase' with its five indented sub-entries). The source text keeps the entry boundaries and the hierarchy. The claim concedes that the entry text and page references match. The only complaint is how a Markdown renderer would show bare lines (as one paragraph) and that the page uses no list markers like pages 961-962. That is a formatting and rendering difference on an informative index page. It changes no content or meaning, so it falls under the formatting-only rejection rule.
